parsed.rationale: Both `ArtistRepository` and `ReleaseRepository` in the `Metadata` package share three identical members — `cacheKey:(for id: Int) -> String`, `entityKind:String`, and `lastSync:Date?` — and differ only in the return type of their `resolve:(id: Int) async throws -> <T>` method (`Artist` vs `Release`). This is the canonical PAT pattern: a family of protocols that are structurally identical except for one varying concrete type. Introducing a `Repository` protocol with `associatedtype Entity` and a `resolve:(id: Int) async throws -> Entity` requirement unifies the two protocols without losing type safety, and the shared members (`cacheKey`, `entityKind`, `lastSync`) move to the parent protocol body. Neither record carries any restraint marker (`is_test`, `is_mock`, `is_sample_app` are all false), so the refactor is safe to apply.
